scheme.name: Documentation of Tiatr through Research Work
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to encourage research work in the field of Tiatr and facilitate writers to take up research work in different aspects of Tiatr, its Song & Music. Research work will be published in book form with remuneration provided to researchers.
scheme.details: The scheme "Documentation of Tiatr through Research Work" was launched by the Tiatr Academy under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to encourage research work in the field of Tiatr and facilitate writers to take up research work in different aspects of Tiatr, its Song & Music. The scheme provides publication of research work in book form with a minimum of 500 copies printed and remuneration as fixed by TAG as per the researcher's experience. The applicant must be a researcher interested in writing books on tiatr after doing thorough research and must submit three typed copies of the manuscript for approval. The scheme is implemented by the Tiatr Academy of Goa (TAG). The applications for this scheme are accepted offline.
scheme.benefits:
> ***Publication Benefits***

- TAG will publish the research work in book form after thorough research on the subject.
- The publication may be in English or Konkani (Roman Script).
- TAG will print a minimum of 500 copies of the book.
- 100 copies will be given to the writer.
- The remaining copies will be used by TAG for various purposes.

> ***Financial Benefits***

The author/researcher will be given remuneration as fixed by TAG as per his/her experience for the research work undertaken.
> ***Editorial Support***

- The manuscript approved by the Recommendation Board shall be edited by a member of Editorial Board.
- Editing will include checking for spelling and orthography.

***Conditions***
_*The manuscript received from the author/researcher will be considered for publication only after getting approval from the Recommendation Board appointed by TAG._
_*The author/researcher will have to provide TAG, 3 (three) typed copies of the manuscript._
_*If approved, the author/researcher will have to submit a soft copy of the manuscript on a Compact Disc/Digital Versatile Disc/pen drive._
scheme.eligibility:
- The applicant must be a researcher interested in writing books on tiatr after doing thorough research on the subject.
- Preference will be given to any researcher who has already done research on any aspect of Tiatr, its Song & Music.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should take a printout of the [prescribed format](https://www.goa.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Citizen-Charter-TAG.pdf) of the application form.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields: name of the applicant, complete address, contact number, email address, Aadhaar Card number, Permanent Account Number Card number, name of the research, and aspects of tiatr on which research is done. Attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). Sign the application form and mention the date.
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to - 
***Tiatr Academy of Goa, AS-1 / AS-4, Block A, 2nd Floor, Campal Trade Centre, Opposite Kala Academy, Campal, Panaji, Goa, India – 403001***
_*Applicants are advised to save a copy of the submitted application form and any acknowledgment_ 

> ***Post-Application Processes***

**Step 1:** _Recommendation Board Review_
The submitted manuscript will be reviewed by the Recommendation Board consisting of 2 members appointed by TAG. The board members will be paid a suitable honorarium as fixed by TAG for the work undertaken.
**Step 2:** _Approval and Soft Copy Submission_
If the manuscript is approved by the Recommendation Board, submit a soft copy of the manuscript on a Compact Disc/Digital Versatile Disc/pen drive to the Tiatr Academy of Goa.
**Step 3:** _Editorial Process_
The approved manuscript will undergo editing by a member of the Editorial Board, which includes checking for spelling and orthography.
**Step 4:** _Publication and Remuneration_
Upon completion of the editorial process, TAG will proceed with printing a minimum of 500 copies of the book and provide remuneration to the author/researcher as per the fixed rates based on experience.

documents_required: Self-Attested Copy of Permanent Account Number Card.
Three Typed Copies of the Manuscript (for approval process).
Soft Copy of the Manuscript on a Compact Disc/Digital Versatile Disc/Pen Drive (if manuscript is approved).

scheme.name: Goa Traditional Bakers (Poders) Subsidy Scheme
scheme.brief_description: "Goa Traditional Bakers (Poders) Subsidy Scheme" aims to provide financial assistance to traditional bakers (poders) in Goa to ensure the protection and growth of this traditional occupation. Subsidies for the purchase of flour are provided to traditional bakers who produce essential Goan breads.
scheme.details: Launched in 2012, the scheme "Goa Traditional Bakers (Poders) Subsidy Scheme" by the Department of Industries, Government of Goa aims to provide financial assistance to traditional bakers (poders) in Goa to ensure the protection and growth of this traditional occupation. Through this scheme, subsidies for the purchase of maida (flour) are provided to traditional bakers who produce essential Goan breads like "Pao," "Undho," "Poie," and "Kakon." The scheme is implemented by the Goa Handicrafts, Rural & Small Scale Industries Development Corporation Ltd. (GHRSSIDC). The objectives of the scheme include maintaining the price of 50gm "Pao" at ₹3 for the next 5 years and supporting bakers who have been in the business for at least 20 years.
scheme.benefits:
The subsidy will be provided for the purchase of maida required for the production of bread, depending on the category the bakers belong to.

- **Category A:** Bakers who use less than or equal to 50 kgs. of maida in a day will get a cash subsidy of ₹4 per kg.- **Category B:** Bakers who use between 51 kgs. to 100 kgs. of maida in a day will get a cash subsidy of ₹4 per kg for the first 50 kgs. and ₹2 per kg for the remaining amount of maida.- **Category C:** Bakers who use between 101 kgs. to 150 kgs. of maida in a day will get a cash subsidy of ₹4 per kg for the first 50 kgs., ₹2 per kg for the next 50 kgs., and ₹1 per kg for the remaining amount of maida.
****The subsidy will be disbursed every quarter.***
****No subsidy for maida beyond the consumption of 150 kgs per day.***
scheme.eligibility:
- The Traditional Goan bakers (poders) who are engaged in the production and selling of Pao, Undho, Poie, Kakon, and similar products will be eligible for availing financial assistance under the scheme as detailed below:
- The existing traditional Bakers/Bakery which are registered with The All Goa Bakers Association registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
- The applicant/his or her family should be engaged in the business of making traditional Goan breads for the last 20 years.
- The baker (poder) should be a Goan resident by birth.
- The traditional baker/poder should be recommended by the All Goa Bakers Association.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** Complete the application form [(Annexure I)](https://dmg.goa.gov.in/PDFs/Notifications/Notification/OFFICIAL%20GAZETTE%20Recognize%20Person%20Notification%20May%202013.pdf) and attach the required documents, including an affidavit declaring the contents of the application as true. 
**Step 2:** Submit the application form along with the required documents to Goa Handicrafts, Rural & Small Scale Industries Development Corporation Ltd. (GHRSSIDC).
_* For quarterly subsidy claims, submit bills of purchase of maida for the relevant quarter along with the application form_ [_(Annexure II)_](https://dmg.goa.gov.in/PDFs/Notifications/Notification/OFFICIAL%20GAZETTE%20Recognize%20Person%20Notification%20May%202013.pdf) _within 30 days of the end of the quarter._
**Appraisal Committee Review**
The Appraisal Committee, consisting of representatives from GHRSSIDC, All Goa Bakers Association, and the Directorate of Industries, Trade & Commerce, will review and sanction the subsidy.

documents_required: Affidavit Sworn By The Applicant Declaring The Contents Mentioned In The Application Are True
Copy Of ID/Registration Of Membership Of Bakers Association
Recommendation From All Goa Bakers Association
Raw Material Purchase Bills For Maida For The Previous 6 Months (From 1st April 2012 to 30th September 2012)
Any one of the following documents as proof that the applicant/his or her family has been engaged in the business of making traditional Goan breads for the last 20 years:
Permanent SSI Unit Registration Or An Acknowledgement Of Entrepreneurship Memorandum Part-II (EM) From The Directorate Of Industries, Trade & Commerce, Government Of Goa
License From the Department Of Legal Metrology Previously (Department Of Weights & Measures)

Certification From Village Panchayat/Municipal Corporation Duly Certified By BDO That The Applicant Is Engaged In The Business For The Last 20 Years Or House Tax/Trade Tax Receipts Of Last 20 Years From Panchayat/Municipality Duly Certified By BDO

faqs.question: As a traditional baker in Goa who wants to receive financial assistance under this scheme, what is the minimum time period I should have been engaged in making traditional Goan breads?
faqs.answer: You must have been engaged in the business of making traditional Goan breads for at least 20 years, and you will need to provide documentation to prove this engagement period.

faqs.question: What types of traditional bread products are eligible for consideration when applying for financial assistance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The eligible traditional bread products include Pao, Undho, Poie, Kakon, and similar products. These must be produced and sold by traditional Goan bakers.

faqs.question: What are the accepted documents I can submit to prove my 20-year engagement in the traditional bread-making business?
faqs.answer: You can submit either a Permanent SSI registration, EM Part-II acknowledgment from Industries Directorate, License from Legal Metrology Department, or certification from Village Panchayat certified by BDO/Municipal Corporation proving 20 years of business.

faqs.question: How does my birth location affect my eligibility for receiving financial assistance as a traditional baker in Goa?
faqs.answer: You must be a Goan resident by birth and must submit your birth certificate as proof. This is a mandatory requirement for eligibility.

faqs.question: As a traditional baker applying for the subsidy, what organization's recommendation do I need to include with my application?
faqs.answer: You must obtain and include a recommendation from the All Goa Bakers Association, which must be registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

faqs.question: I use 45 kilograms of maida per day in my bakery. What category would I fall under and how much subsidy would I receive?
faqs.answer: You would fall under Category A ([?]50 kg maida per day) and would be eligible for a cash subsidy of Rs. 4 per kg for your daily maida usage.

faqs.question: If my daily maida consumption is 80 kilograms, what would be my subsidy calculation under this scheme?
faqs.answer: You would fall under Category B (51-100 kg) and receive Rs. 4 per kg for the first 50 kg and Rs. 2 per kg for the remaining 30 kg of maida.

faqs.question: How will my subsidy be calculated if I use 120 kilograms of maida daily in my traditional bakery?
faqs.answer: You would fall under Category C (101-150 kg) and receive Rs. 4 per kg for first 50 kg, Rs. 2 per kg for next 50 kg, and Rs. 1 per kg for remaining 20 kg.

faqs.question: What is the maximum daily maida consumption limit beyond which no subsidy will be provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No subsidy will be provided for maida consumption beyond 150 kilograms per day. This is the absolute upper limit for subsidy calculation.

faqs.question: How frequently can I submit my subsidy claims and what is the timeline for submitting the bills after each quarter?
faqs.answer: Claims can be submitted quarterly (Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep, Oct-Dec, Jan-Mar), and bills must be submitted within 30 days of the end of each relevant quarter.

faqs.question: From which suppliers should I purchase maida to be eligible for claiming subsidy under this scheme?
faqs.answer: You must purchase maida from government marketing federations or marketing co-operative societies like Sahakar Bhandar, Bardez Bazar, or Goa Bhagyatdar as approved by GHRSSIDC.

faqs.question: What is the government's objective regarding the pricing of 50-gram Pao, and for how long will this price be maintained?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to maintain the price of 50-gram Pao at Rs. 3, valid for 5 years, after which the government may review the price.

scheme.name: The Goa State Photo Contest And Exhibition Scheme
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to encourage local youths in photography and photojournalism, providing cash prizes and exhibition opportunities. The scheme offers cash prizes of ₹20,000/-, ₹16,000/-, and ₹12,000/- in each category. Entries from applicants born and residing in Goa are preferred.
scheme.details: "The Goa State Photo Contest And Exhibition Scheme" by the Department of Information & Publicity, Government of Goa, aims to encourage young talents in photography and photojournalism, promote self-employment, and provide a platform for local youths to exhibit their work. The scheme offers cash prizes of ₹20,000/-, ₹16,000/-, and ₹12,000/- in each category. Benefits also include exhibitions for selected entries. Applicants born and residing in Goa for at least 15 years are given preference.
scheme.benefits:
- First prize: ₹20,000/- in each category.
- Second prize: ₹16,000/- in each category.
- Third prize: ₹12,000/- in each category.
- Five consolation prizes: ₹2,000/- each.
- Certificates are presented to the best entries.
- Judges' Honorarium: ₹5,000/- each for three judges.
scheme.exclusions:
- The applicant must not be an employee of the Department of Information & Publicity.
- Mobile images are not accepted.
scheme.eligibility: Individuals who were born and residing in Goa for 15 years or more will be given preference, though the scheme does not bar others.

application_process.steps: The interested individuals should send their entries along with the required documents and details to the "Director of Information & Publicity, 3rd Floor, Udyog Bhavan, Panaji, Goa", superscribing the envelope as “Entries for The Goa State Photo Contest And Exhibition”. A soft copy of high-resolution photographs will also be required to be submitted.

documents_required: Author Details: Name, Nationality, Postal Address, Mobile Number, Telephone Number, and Email Address (Written on the Back of Photographs in Block Letters).
Technical Details of the Camera Used.
Brief Description of Each Photograph (Not More Than 50 Words).
Bio-data of the Photographer (Not More Than 100 Words).
Certificate of Originality (Declaring Photographs as Original Work).
Latest Residence Certificate (as Proof of Eligibility).

faqs.question: What are the two categories for the photo contest and what topics do they cover?
faqs.answer: The first category is "Unknown Tourist Spot in Goa," and the second category is "Promoting Self Employment to sustain livelihood."

faqs.question: What personal details must be included on the back of each submitted photograph?
faqs.answer: The photographer’s name, nationality, postal address, mobile/telephone numbers, and email address must be written in block letters on the back of each photograph.

faqs.question: Are mobile phone images acceptable for submission in the contest?
faqs.answer: No, mobile phone images will not be considered for entry in the contest.

faqs.question: What technical details about the photograph must accompany the submission?
faqs.answer: The entrant must provide details such as the camera used along with the photograph submission.

faqs.question: Is there a word limit for the brief description of the photograph and the photographer’s bio-data?
faqs.answer: Yes, the brief description of the photograph and the photographer’s bio-data must not exceed 100 words each.

faqs.question: What certification is required to confirm the originality of the submitted photographs?
faqs.answer: The entrant must provide a certificate stating that all photographs are original works taken by the entrant themselves.

faqs.question: Are soft copies of the photographs required for submission?
faqs.answer: Yes, entrants must submit a soft copy along with a high-resolution version of the photograph.

faqs.question: What are the size and color requirements for the printed photographs?
faqs.answer: Entrants must submit color prints in 12 x 8 size for the contest.

faqs.question: How many photographs can an entrant submit for the contest?
faqs.answer: An entrant can submit a maximum of 4 different photographs, either in one or both categories.

faqs.question: Is there an entry fee or age restriction for participating in the contest?
faqs.answer: No, there is no entry fee, age bar, or qualification required for participation.

faqs.question: Are photographs taken using drones eligible for submission?
faqs.answer: No, pictures shot with drones will not be accepted in the contest.

faqs.question: What are the cash prizes for the first, second, and third prizes in each category?
faqs.answer: The first prize is ₹20,000, the second prize is ₹16,000, and the third prize is ₹12,000 in each category.

faqs.question: Are there any consolation prizes, and what is their value?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are five consolation prizes of ₹2,000 each in each category.

faqs.question: Will the submitted photographs remain the property of the entrant after submission?
faqs.answer: No, the photographs will become the property of the Department of Information and Publicity and may be used for exhibitions or publications.

scheme.name: Financial Assistance for Purchase of Fuel (Petrol) to the Fishermen for Operation of Out Board Motors
scheme.brief_description: The scheme “Financial Assistance for Purchase of Fuel (Petrol) to the Fishermen for Operation of Out Board Motors” is a scheme by the Department of Fisheries, Government of Goa. Through this scheme, a subsidy of ₹30 per Litre on a maximum consumption of 1700 Litre of Petrol is provided to fishermen.
scheme.details: The scheme “Financial Assistance for Purchase of Fuel (Petrol) to the Fishermen for Operation of Out Board Motors” is a scheme by the Department of Fisheries, Government of Goa. Through this scheme, a subsidy of ₹ 30 per Litre on a maximum consumption of 1000 Litre of Petrol is provided to the fishermen.
scheme.benefits:
- Subsidy of ₹ 30 per Litre on a maximum consumption of 1000 Litre of Petrol.
- For SC/ST, a Subsidy of ₹ 30 per Litre on a maximum consumption of 1100 Litre of Petrol.

- The benefits can be availed every year.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant should be a traditional fisherman by birth or profession.
1. The applicant should be a resident of Goa.
1. The applicant's fishing canoe should be registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, of 1958 and the rules framed there under.
1. The applicant should be a member of the Registered Fisheries Co-operative Societies/ Association or Individual.
1. The applicant should not be a defaulter of the Directorate of Fisheries.
1. The applicant should not be a violator of the Goa Daman & Diu Marine Fishing Regulation Act,1980 (Act No.3 of 1981).
1. Petrol OBM (Out Board Motors) having 10HP or below should be incorporated on the Fishing Vessel/Canoe.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should take print of the [prescribed format](https://fisheries.goa.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/F.R.P.-Application-forms.pdf) of the application form.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the concerned authority at the **Department of Fisheries, Dayanand Bandodkar Marg, Patto Colony, Panaji Goa - 403 521, or to the official posted at** [BDO Office/ Sub-Offices](https://fisheries.goa.gov.in/contact-us-2/#) **of the Department of Fisheries.**

> **Grievance Redressal**

Any dissatisfaction or complaint about any service or its standards can be registered with the Department's [Grievance Redressal Officer](https://fisheries.goa.gov.in/contact-us-2/#). The grievance can also be lodged on the link **dir-fish.goa@nic.in**. All complaints will be acknowledged by us and final action taken will be communicated within 30 days.

documents_required: Certificate of Vessel Registration, with OBM (Out Board Motors) incorporated on it, issued by the Directorate of Fisheries, Government of Goa, under the Merchant Shipping Act 1958.
Fishing Vessel License Certificate, issued under the Goa, Daman & Diu Marine Fishing Regulation Rules 1982.
Fishing Net License Certificate, issued under the Goa Fisheries Rule 1981.
Original bill (may be submitted by the owner of the petrol pump).
Petrol Consumption Passbook maintained by Registered Fisheries Cooperative Societies/ Association/ Individuals.

faqs.question: Are there any penalties or disqualifications mentioned for defaulters or violators of specific acts?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant should not be a defaulter of the Directorate of Fisheries or a violator of the Goa Daman & Diu Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980.

faqs.question: Can the application form be submitted online, or is it only accepted in person?
faqs.answer: As per the guidelines, the filled and signed application form, along with documents, should be submitted to the Directorate of Fisheries or designated offices.

faqs.question: Can an applicant apply for the scheme if their fishing canoe is not registered under the Merchant Shipping Act?
faqs.answer: No, eligibility criteria include the fishing canoe being registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, and the rules framed thereunder.

faqs.question: Is There Any Compensation For The Delay In The Disbursal Of The Scheme Benefits?
faqs.answer: Unfortunately, there is no compensation specified for the delay in disbursal of scheme benefits.

faqs.question: Can Applicants From The Neighboring States Also Apply To This Scheme?
faqs.answer: No, this scheme is exclusively for permanent residents of the state. Neighboring state applicants are not eligible.

faqs.question: Is there an application deadline for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The information does not specify an application deadline.

faqs.question: Are there any specific provisions for persons with disabilities under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The information does not mention specific provisions for persons with disabilities.

faqs.question: What actions are taken to address grievances registered with the Department's Grievance Redressal Officer?
faqs.answer: All complaints will be acknowledged, and final actions will be communicated within 30 days.

faqs.question: Can individuals with Petrol Out Board Motors above 10HP apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme specifies that only Petrol OBM with 10HP or below should be incorporated on the Fishing Vessel/Canoe.

faqs.question: What is the maximum petrol consumption limit for SC/ST beneficiaries under the scheme?
faqs.answer: SC/ST beneficiaries have a maximum allowable petrol consumption of 1100 litres, with a subsidy of [?]30 per litre.

faqs.question: How can one contact the Grievance Redressal Officer for the Department?
faqs.answer: The Grievance Redressal Officer can be contacted through the email dir-fish.goa@nic.in or by registering complaints on the provided link.

faqs.question: Can you provide details on the location for submitting the application form?
faqs.answer: The filled application form and documents should be submitted to the Directorate of Fisheries, Dayanand Bandodkar Marg, Panaji Goa, or at the designated BDO Office/ Sub-Offices.

faqs.question: Is there a restriction on the horsepower of Petrol Out Board Motors (OBM) incorporated on the Fishing Vessel/Canoe?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme specifies that Petrol OBM of 10HP or below should be incorporated on the Fishing Vessel/Canoe.

faqs.question: How frequently can a beneficiary avail themselves of the benefits outlined in the scheme?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary is entitled to avail these benefits every year.

scheme.name: Goa Village & Municipal Child Committee Grants And Awards Scheme
scheme.brief_description: GVMCCGS awards the Panchayats / Municipal Local Bodies to discuss and resolve the issues relating to children. The winner is awarded an annual financial grant of ₹ 10,000/- towards administrative expenses incurred on organizing the activities of the Committee.
scheme.details: Introduced in the year 2015-16, the scheme "Goa Village & Municipal Child Committee Grants and Awards Scheme (GVMCCGS)" covers all the Village and Municipal Child Committees set up under [Rule 7 of The Goa Children's Homes Rules, 2004](https://dwcd.goa.gov.in/uploads/The%20Goa%20Childrens%20Rules.pdf) by the local bodies as per provisions of the rules. The winner is awarded an annual financial grant of ₹ 10,000/- towards administrative expenses incurred on organizing the activities of the Committee. The applicant should be the concerned local body i.e. a Panchayat or a Municipal Local Body.
scheme.benefits:
**Amount:** An annual financial grant of ₹ 10,000/- towards administrative expenses incurred on organizing the activities of the Committee.
**Instalments:** The grant will be released in a single instalment within three months. 
**Mode:** All payments will be made only through electronic transfers favouring the local body concerned.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant should be the concerned local body i.e. a Panchayat or a Municipal local body.
1. The applicant should have established a Village or Municipal Child Committee as prescribed under [Rule 7 of The Goa Children's Homes Rules, 2004](https://dwcd.goa.gov.in/uploads/The%20Goa%20Childrens%20Rules.pdf).1. The Committee should have met at least once in the last three months prior to submission of the application.
1. The Committee should have met to discuss and resolve the issues relating to children within the jurisdiction of the local body.
1. The concerned local body should have provided the space for facilitating sittings of the Committee in its premises as and when required.

application_process.steps:
The application as per the prescribed format (made available at the time of the release of the press note), along with the supporting documents showing the activities of the Child Committee of the Local Body, shall be addressed/submitted directly to:
**The Director, Directorate of Women And Child Development, Panaji-Goa, 2nd floor, Old Education Building, 18th June Road, Altinho, Panaji, Goa - 403 001.**

> **Applicant**

The application should be submitted only by the following - 
1. **The Village Panchayat.**
 (a) The proposal be signed by its Secretary, along with the resolution of the Panchayat Body.
 (b) The proposal should be duly recommended by the concerned Block Development Officer.
2. **The Municipality.**
 (a) The proposal be signed by its Chief Executive, along with the resolution of the body. 

> **Deadline**

The application shall be submitted within six months from the commencement of the financial year.

documents_required: Documents showing the activities of the Child Committee.

faqs.question: What Happens If The Selection Committee Does Not Find Any Suitable Child Committee For An Award In A Particular Taluka?
faqs.answer: If the Selection Committee does not find any Child Committee that meets the criteria for receiving the award in a specific taluka, no award shall be given in that taluka.

faqs.question: What Is The Significance Of The Director Of Women & Child Development In The GVMCCGS Grant Process?
faqs.answer: The Director of Women & Child Development holds the position of the competent Sanctioning Authority for the grants under the GVMCCGS. This authority is responsible for sanctioning the financial grants to the eligible local bodies based on the recommendations made by the Selection Committee.

faqs.question: Who Constitutes The Selection Committee For The GVMCCGS Awards, And What Is Their Role In The Selection Process?
faqs.answer: The Selection Committee is comprised of the Chairperson, who is the Secretary (WCD), and the Member Secretary, who is the Director of Women & Child Development. Additionally, two Social Workers nominated by the Government are part of the committee. Their role is to scrutinize and adjudge the best performing Child Committee for each taluka and recommend them for the release of the award.

faqs.question: Can The GVMCCGS Grant Be Availed In Multiple Installments?
faqs.answer: No, the GVMCCGS grant will be released in a single instalment within three months.

faqs.question: Can You Explain The Purpose Of The Village And Municipal Child Committees Established Under Rule 7 Of The Goa Children's Homes Rules, 2004?
faqs.answer: The Village and Municipal Child Committees are established to discuss and resolve issues relating to children within the jurisdiction of the local body as per the provisions of Rule 7 of The Goa Children's Homes Rules, 2004.

faqs.question: Are There Any Specific Requirements For The Space Provided By The Local Body For The Child Committee?
faqs.answer: The local body should provide the space for facilitating sittings of the Child Committee in its premises as and when required.

faqs.question: Can You Explain The Purpose Of The Financial Grant Provided Under The GVMCCGS?
faqs.answer: The financial grant of [?]10,000/- provided under the GVMCCGS is meant to cover the administrative expenses incurred on organizing the activities of the Child Committee.

faqs.question: What Is The Mode Of Payment For The GVMCCGS Grant?
faqs.answer: All payments will be made only through electronic transfers favouring the concerned local body.

faqs.question: How Is The Selection Process Conducted For The GVMCCGS Awards?
faqs.answer:
The Selection Committee Chaired by Secretary (WCD) and Director, WCD being its Member Secretary along with two Social Workers to be nominated by the Government shall scrutinize and adjudge the best performing Child Committee for each taluka and recommend them for release of the award.
The Director, Women & Child Development shall be the competent Sanctioning Authority for these grants.

faqs.question: What Documents Need To Be Submitted Along With The GVMCCGS Application?
faqs.answer: Documents showing the activities of the Child Committee.

faqs.question: Can You Clarify The Deadline For Submitting The GVMCCGS Application?
faqs.answer: The application shall be submitted within six months from the commencement of the financial year.

faqs.question: How Can A Local Body Apply For The GVMCCGS Grant?
faqs.answer:
The application as per the prescribed format (made available at the time of the release of the press note), along with the supporting documents showing the activities of the Child Committee of the Local Body shall be addressed/submitted directly to:
The Director, Directorate of Women And Child Development, Panaji-Goa, 2nd floor, Old Education Building, 18th June Road, Altinho, Panaji, Goa - 403 001.

scheme.name: Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme
scheme.department: Startup Promotion Cell (SPC)
scheme.brief_description: Through “Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme”, in case of land/ developed area purchased/ leased by Start-ups/ incubators/ accelerators, the stamp duty for land area lease/ sale transaction for start-ups/incubators/ accelerators will not exceed ₹ 100/-, and the excess amount paid will be reimbursed.
scheme.details: The scheme “Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme” is a scheme by the Department of Information Technology, Electronics and Communications, Government of Goa, for the Startups of Goa. Through this scheme, in case of land/ developed area purchased/ leased by Start-ups/ incubators/ accelerators, the stamp duty for land area lease/ sale transaction for start-ups/incubators/ accelerators will not exceed ₹ 100/-, and the excess amount paid to the authorities concerned will be reimbursed.
scheme.benefits:
1. In case of land/ developed area purchased/ leased by Start-ups/ incubators/ accelerators, the stamp duty for land area lease/ sale transaction for start-ups/incubators/ accelerators will not exceed ₹ 100/-, and the excess amount paid to the authorities concerned will be reimbursed.
1. A start-up is eligible only once to avail the benefits of this scheme.
1. In the case of an incubator/accelerator, this amount shall be paid after a period of three years of successful operation. This can be relaxed in the case of a company that is in the business of making incubators.
1. Up to 100 start-ups can avail the benefits of this scheme per year.

**NOTE:** Under no circumstance shall the benefits under this scheme be considered an entitlement.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant should be a Start-up certified by the Start-up Promotion Cell (SPC) and incubators/accelerators enlisted with the Start-up Promotion Cell (SPC).
1. The applicant can apply for this scheme only once in their lifetime.
1. The bank accounts of the Directors of the company should be linked to Aadhaar.
1. Only expenditures incurred from one year before the notification of Goa Start-up Policy 2017, being within the validity of this policy and paid for digitally would be considered for reimbursement. In case digital payments are not possible then it shall be up to the SPC as per its due diligence to admit the expenditure.
1. A start-up can avail of the benefits of this scheme only once.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** Visit the [Official Website](https://goaonline.gov.in/public/startuplogin?) of Goa Startup Mission.
**Step 2:** Verify your Email ID and Mobile Number using OTP. You will be redirected to the Registration Page.
**Step 3:** On the [Registration/Signup Page](https://goaonline.gov.in/Public/stpRegistration_af), fill in all the mandatory fields of the registration form (Country, Name, Date of Birth, Address, PIN Code, Gender, etc.).
**Step 4:** Create a Login Name and a strong Password (Password can have special characters like @ # $ % ^ & + =).
**Step 5:** Carefully read the Declaration and the Terms & Conditions, and tick the checkboxes.
**Step 6:** Fill in the Captcha Code, and click "Register/Signup".
**Step 7:** Login to the website using your Login Name and Password. Fill in the Captcha Code, and click "Login".
**Step 8:** Navigate to the online application form for the relevant scheme.
**Step 9:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload all the mandatory documents (self-attest if required).
**Step 10:** Submit the application and note the application reference number for application tracking.

**OR** 

**Step 1:** Take a print of the [proforma](https://www.goa.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/Schemes.pdf) of the application form. Fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest if required).
**Step 2:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to SPC via Email at spc-dit.goa@gov.in

**NOTE:** The applicant can apply for this scheme at any time of the financial year but only within 6 months of incurring the relevant expenditure.

> **Evaluation Process**

**Step 1:** On receipt of the complete application, the SPC shall inspect and verify the contents of the application. Based on the received documents, SPC will scrutinize and perform necessary due diligence on the expenses incurred by the applicant.
**Step 2:** The SPC shall recommend the application for the sanction of reimbursement of the costs incurred towards filing or grant of IP as the case may be. 

> **Notification**

The applications received by the SPC shall be evaluated and approval or rejection shall be notified within 45 days from receipt of the application by the SPC.

documents_required: Original Proof of Payment of Stamp Duty

faqs.question: What is the maximum stamp duty for land area lease/sale transactions under the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme for Goa startups?
faqs.answer: The stamp duty for such transactions will not exceed [?]100, with the excess amount reimbursed.

faqs.question: Can the three-year successful operation requirement be relaxed for a company making incubators under the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, this requirement can be relaxed for such companies.

faqs.question: How many start-ups per year can benefit from the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme in Goa?
faqs.answer: Up to 100 start-ups can avail the scheme's benefits annually.

faqs.question: Is the benefit under the scheme considered an entitlement for eligible start-ups and incubators/accelerators?
faqs.answer: No, the benefits under this scheme are not considered entitlements under any circumstances.

faqs.question: When can the stamp duty reimbursement amount be paid in the case of an incubator/accelerator under the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme?
faqs.answer: The amount shall be paid after three years of successful operation, with possible relaxation for companies engaged in making incubators.

faqs.question: Can a start-up apply more than once for the benefits under the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme?
faqs.answer: No, a start-up is eligible only once to avail of the benefits of this scheme.

faqs.question: What is the timeline considered for reimbursable expenditures under the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme?
faqs.answer: Only expenditures paid digitally from one year before the notification of Goa Start-up Policy 2017 until the policy's validity are considered for reimbursement.

faqs.question: In case digital payments are not possible, how are expenditures considered for reimbursement under the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme?
faqs.answer: If digital payments are not possible, it is up to the SPC, following due diligence, to admit the expenditure.

faqs.question: Can other documents be attached to the application for the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, if attaching other documents, they should be mentioned, but the listed mandatory documents are essential.

faqs.question: What role does the SPC play in the Stamp Duty Reimbursement Scheme application process?
faqs.answer: The SPC conducts due diligence, makes decisions on eligibility, and may prohibit individuals from availing scheme benefits in case of misrepresentation or fraudulent activity.

scheme.name: Scheme to Provide Grant to the Institutions for Long Term Project in the Field of Art and Culture (Sarjansheel Goa)
scheme.brief_description: "Scheme to Provide Grant to the Institutions for Long Term Project in the Field of Art and Culture (Sarjansheel Goa)" implemented by the by the Directorate of Art and Culture, provides financial support to the institutions/ individuals involved in long-term projects in the field Art & Culture.
scheme.details:
"Scheme to Provide Grant to the Institutions for Long Term Project in the Field of Art and Culture (Sarjansheel Goa)" implemented by the by the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa, provides financial support to the institutions/ individuals involved in long-term projects in the field of Art & Culture.

> **Objectives**

1. To create and develop a cultural environment in the State of Goa. 
1. To provide financial support to the institutions/ individuals involved in long-term projects in the field of Art and culture. 
1. To preserve and promote the cultural heritage of Goa.
scheme.benefits:
A grant to the extent of 80% of the total expenditure involved is subject to a maximum ceiling of ₹ 5,00,000 per annum. 

> **Number of Beneficiaries**

The Department/Government may restrict the number of institutions/individuals according to the availability of funds.
scheme.eligibility:
> **For Institutions** 

1. Any institution registered under the Society’s Registration Act, 1860 or Indian Trust Act. 
1. The institution must be involved in long-term projects in the field of Art and Culture.

> **For Individuals**

1. Any individual from the Goan community, who has been a resident of Goa for 15 years or more.
1. The individual must be involved in a long-term project in the field of Art and Culture and should have contributed at least 15 years in the relevant field.

application_process.steps:

**Step 2:** Request a hard copy of the proforma from the concerned authority.

documents_required: A copy of the Constitution/By-laws/ Rules and Regulations.
An audited statement of accounts of the last 3 proceeding years duly signed by the Chartered Accountant.
Detailed project report of that particular long-term project for which financial support is asked under this scheme.
A copy of the Residence Certificate of 15 years or more in Goa.
