scheme.name: Krishak Utpadak Kshati Sahayata Yojana
scheme.department: Uttarakhand Agricultural Production & Marketing Board
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance and compensation to farmers in the event of loss or damage to crops, livestock, or agricultural land caused by fire, flood, or heavy rains in the notified areas of the state.
scheme.details: The scheme “Krishak Utpadak Kshati Sahayata Yojana” is implemented by the Uttarakhand Agricultural Production & Marketing Board under the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance and compensation to farmers in the event of loss or damage to crops, livestock, or agricultural land caused by fire, flood, or heavy rains in the notified areas of the state.
scheme.benefits: Damage caused by fire accidents to standing crops, harvested crops in the field, crops stored in barns for threshing, or residual produce in the notified market areas of Uttarakhand State, as well as damage to property and livestock due to fire in the farmer’s house, and damage to agricultural land due to floods or rain-induced soil erosion, all such losses make farmers eligible to receive compensation under this scheme.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a minimum of 18 years of age to submit and receive a claim.

application_process.steps:
- For reporting fire or flood accidents, the affected farmer/producer must submit an application in the prescribed format (available free of cost at the Mandi Samiti office) to the Secretary, Chairman, Administrator, or Tehsildar of the concerned Mandi Samiti area within seven days of the incident.
 - The received claim will be investigated by the Secretary of the Market Committee, and the inquiry must be completed within one week. The final report shall be submitted to the Chairman/Administrator of the Mandi Committee in the prescribed format attached to the claim form. In areas where the Mandi Committee does not have an office, the concerned Tehsildar will conduct the inquiry and forward it to the respective Mandi Committee.
 - After thorough scrutiny of the claim form by the Mandi Samiti office, the payment process will be initiated with the approval of the Chairman/Administrator of the Mandi Samiti.
 - All the above proceedings should be completed within two months, and in special circumstances, the Chairman/Administrator of the Mandi Committee may extend the time period as required.
 - For the payment of assistance claims, the Mandi Board will prepare a bank draft of the sanctioned amount in the name of the claimant and send it to the Secretary of the concerned Mandi Committee for disbursement.

documents_required: Documents are required in accordance with the Mandi Committee/ Mandi Board for claiming the compensation under the scheme.

faqs.question: Who can benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: All resident farmers and agricultural producers of Uttarakhand who suffer damage to crops, livestock, or agricultural property due to fire, flood, or heavy rains in the notified market areas can benefit from this scheme.

faqs.question: What types of damages are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer:
The scheme covers:

- Fire damage to standing crops, harvested crops, or crops kept in barns for threshing.
- Damage to property and livestock due to fire in the farmer’s house.
- Damage to agricultural land due to floods or rain-induced soil erosion.

faqs.question: Is there any age limit to apply for compensation?
faqs.answer: Yes, the minimum age to apply for compensation under the scheme is 18 years.

faqs.question: Where can farmers get the application form?
faqs.answer: Farmers can obtain the application form free of cost from the concerned Mandi Samiti office.

faqs.question: Within how many days must the incident be reported?
faqs.answer: The affected farmer or producer must report the incident within 7 days of its occurrence by submitting the application form.

faqs.question: To whom should the application be submitted?
faqs.answer: The application should be submitted to the Secretary, Chairman, Administrator, or Tehsildar of the concerned Mandi Samiti area.

faqs.question: How is the compensation amount paid to the farmer?
faqs.answer: The Mandi Board prepares a bank draft in the name of the claimant and sends it to the Secretary of the concerned Mandi Committee for disbursement to the farmer.

scheme.name: Right to Education Act 2009 - Uttarakhand
scheme.department: Secondary Education Department, Government Of Uttarakhand
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide free education, textbooks, uniforms, and the benefits of the PM Poshan Yojana to children up to Class 8 in private schools, targeting rural and urban children from weaker and deprived sections of Uttarakhand.
scheme.details: The “Right to Education Act 2009” is implemented under the Samagra Shiksha Programme by the Secondary Education Department, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide free education, textbooks, uniforms, and the benefits of the PM Poshan Yojana to children up to Class 8 in private schools, targeting rural and urban children from weaker and deprived sections of Uttarakhand.
scheme.benefits:
- Under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act, children from weaker and disadvantaged sections in rural and urban areas of Uttarakhand are provided free education, textbooks, uniforms, and the benefits of the PM Poshan Yojana up to Class 8 in private schools.
 - In private schools, 25% of the total seats in the entry-level class are reserved for children from weaker and disadvantaged sections under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act.
scheme.eligibility:
**Children from the following categories will be eligible for admission up to Class 8 in private schools:**

 1. **Children from weaker sections:** Those whose parents/guardians have an annual income of ₹55,000/- or less, or are BPL card holders. 1. **Children from disadvantaged classes:** SC, ST, and children belonging to the non-creamy layer of OBC, with a family annual income of up to ₹4.5 lakh. 1. Orphan children.
 1. Children with physical disabilities.
 1. Children living with HIV/AIDS or those dependent on parents who are HIV/AIDS positive.
 1. Children dependent on disabled parents or parents affected by leprosy, with a family annual income of less than ₹4.5 lakh.
 1. Children dependent on a divorced or widowed mother, with an annual family income of less than ₹80,000/-.

application_process.steps:
Online applications are invited through an advertisement issued in February-March. Parents or guardians can apply online through the official portal or with the help of a cyber café.

 1. Before applying, the following documents are mandatory for children from weaker and disadvantaged sections: passport-size photograph of the child, Aadhaar card of the child and parents/guardians, caste certificate, permanent residence certificate, BPL certificate or income certificate (as applicable), disability certificate (if applicable), husband’s death certificate (in case of widow), divorce certificate (in case of divorcee), and orphan certificate (if applicable).
 1. After filling in the address details on the portal, the parent/guardian can view the list of schools available in their ward and must select the nearest school. Once the form is submitted online, a printout of the application, along with self-attested copies of the required documents, must be submitted to the office of the concerned Deputy Education Officer / Block Education Officer.
 1. All submitted documents are verified by a committee at the development block level. The details of students found eligible are updated and verified on the online portal.
 1. If the number of applications exceeds the available seats in private schools, the selection of children is done through an online lottery conducted at the state level.

documents_required: Aadhaar card of the child and parents/guardians
BPL certificate / Income certificate (as applicable under eligibility)
Husband’s death certificate (in case of widow)

faqs.answer: Eligible children receive free education, textbooks, uniforms, and the benefits of the PM Poshan Yojana.

faqs.answer: Children are eligible for free education and benefits up to Class 8 in private schools.

faqs.answer: Applications are generally invited through advertisements in February-March each year.

faqs.answer: Applications can be submitted online through the official portal, either directly or via a cyber café.

faqs.answer: All documents are verified by a committee at the development block level.

faqs.question: What happens if the number of applications is greater than the available seats?
faqs.answer: If applications exceed available seats, children are selected through an online lottery conducted at the state level.

scheme.name: Investment Grant for Farmers with More than 2 Hectares of Agricultural Land
scheme.department: Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to farmers owning more than 2 hectares of agricultural land who suffer crop losses due to natural disasters.
scheme.details: The scheme “Investment Grant for Farmers with More than 2 Hectares of Agricultural Land” is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority under the Department of Disaster Management, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to farmers owning more than 2 hectares of agricultural land who suffer crop losses due to natural disasters.
scheme.benefits:
Under this scheme:

 1. ₹8,500/- per hectare for unirrigated areas.
 1. ₹17,000/- per hectare for areas with assured irrigation.
 1. ₹22,500/- per hectare for all types of evergreen crops. 

In cases where crop damage exceeds 33%, assistance will be provided only up to a maximum limit of 2 hectares per farmer.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident farmer of Uttarakhand engaged in agricultural activities within the state.
 1. The financial assistance will be applicable only for the area actually sown with crops.

application_process.steps: Information about the disaster and the resulting damage is received from various sources. The concerned Patwari verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form. The Patwari’s report is subsequently verified by the Tehsildar and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Approval is then obtained from the District Magistrate. Once the District Magistrate’s approval is received, relief funds are disbursed to the concerned beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.

documents_required: Form P-20 Entry Confirmation (recorded by the concerned Patwari)

faqs.question: Who is eligible to receive benefits under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers owning more than 2 hectares of agricultural land who have suffered crop damage due to a recognized natural disaster are eligible.

faqs.question: What type of financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides an investment grant per hectare based on the type of land and crop cultivated.

faqs.question: What is the rate of assistance for unirrigated areas?
faqs.answer: For unirrigated areas, financial assistance of ₹8,500/- per hectare is provided.

faqs.question: What is the rate of assistance for areas with assured irrigation?
faqs.answer: For areas with assured irrigation, financial assistance of ₹17,000/- per hectare is provided.

faqs.question: What is the rate of assistance for evergreen crops?
faqs.answer: For evergreen crops, farmers receive ₹22,500/- per hectare as investment support.

faqs.question: Is there a maximum limit of land area for which assistance is payable?
faqs.answer: Yes. Even if a farmer owns more than 2 hectares, assistance will be payable only up to a maximum of 2 hectares per farmer.

faqs.question: Is assistance given for all types of land or only sown areas?
faqs.answer: Assistance is payable only for the sown area where the crop loss has occurred.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for verifying the crop damage?
faqs.answer: The concerned Patwari verifies the crop damage in affected areas and records the details in the P-20 form.

faqs.question: What is the process after the Patwari’s verification?
faqs.answer: After the Patwari verifies and records the damage, the report is verified by the Tehsildar and then by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) for further approval.

scheme.name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban: Individual House Construction Component - Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) Uttarakhand
scheme.department: Nagar Nigam Dehradun
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to eligible urban families for constructing a pucca house on their own land or for improving their existing kutcha or weak houses.
scheme.details: The “Individual House Construction Component – Beneficiary Led Construction” scheme is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban), implemented by the Nagar Nigam Dehradun under the Department of Urban Development, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to eligible urban families for constructing a pucca house on their own land or for improving their existing kutcha or weak houses.
scheme.benefits:
- Under the scheme, a grant of ₹2 lakh is provided to approved beneficiaries in installments, based on the progress of housing construction. Of this amount, ₹50,000/- is provided by the State Government and ₹1,50,000/- by the Government of India.
 - As per Hon’ble Chief Minister’s Announcement No. 458/2022, beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) are provided an additional incentive of ₹5,000/- for home decoration upon completion of the house.
scheme.eligibility:
The following are the eligibility criteria to avail the benefits of the scheme:

 1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The applicant must have been residing in the city from which he/she wishes to receive the benefit on or before 17th June 2015.
 1. The applicant, or any member of their family, must not own a house in their name anywhere in India. (Here, a house refers to a habitable unit suitable for all-weather living.)
 1. The annual family income must not exceed ₹3 lakh.
 1. The applicant must not have received any benefit for residential housing under any other Central, State, or externally aided scheme.
 1. The applicant must have a legally owned plot of land or an existing kutcha/weak residential structure on which they wish to construct a pucca house.

application_process.steps:
To avail the benefits of the scheme, interested persons/families can visit the Municipal Body office according to their housing demand and eligibility, and register their demand for free housing along with the following documents/legal land ownership records:

 1. Aadhaar card of all family members as identity proof.
 1. Proof of residence in the city before 17th June 2015 (such as electricity bill, water bill, telephone bill, voter ID, Aadhaar card, ration card, passport, or any other authentic document).
 1. Bank account in the name of an adult female member of the beneficiary family; in the absence of an adult female member, the account may be in the name of a male member.
 1. Certified copy of legal land ownership records (Registry/Khasra/Khatauni/Patta, etc.), which should be verified both physically and documentarily.
 1. Valid Income Certificate or self-declared income on a ₹10/- stamp paper.
 1. Caste certificate, photocopy of BPL card, or disability certificate.
 1. Notarized affidavit on a ₹10/- stamp paper based on the following eligibility criteria:

 - Has been residing in the municipal area since 17th June 2015 or earlier.
 - Does not own a permanent house in his or her name or in the name of any family member anywhere in India. (Beneficiary family includes husband, wife, and their unmarried sons or daughters.)
 - The annual income of the family does not exceed ₹3 lakh.
 - Has not availed any benefit for residential housing under any other Central, State, or externally aided scheme.

8. Selection of beneficiaries is done after examining and verifying the above records and documents. All details are mandatorily recorded on the official website of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Urban ([www.pmaymis.gov.in](https://pmaymis.gov.in/)). A survey code is issued after registering a housing demand on the portal. This code is compiled with a list of eligible beneficiaries and sent to the Government of India through the State Government for approval. After receiving approval from the Government of India, the beneficiary is granted the housing benefit. There is a free application process to avail the scheme's benefits.

documents_required: Aadhaar card of all family members as identity proof
Proof of residence in the city before 17th June 2015 (such as electricity bill, water bill, telephone bill, voter ID, Aadhaar card, ration card, passport, or any other authentic document).
Bank account in the name of an adult female member of the beneficiary family; in the absence of an adult female member, the account may be in the name of a male member.

Notarized affidavit on a ₹10 stamp paper

faqs.question: Who can apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Urban families who meet the eligibility criteria, including residency in the city before 17th June 2015, income limits, and ownership of land or a kutcha house, can apply.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Approved beneficiaries receive ₹2 lakh in installments based on the progress of housing construction – ₹1.5 lakh from the Government of India and ₹50,000/- from the State Government.

faqs.question: Is there any additional incentive under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, as per Chief Minister’s Announcement No. 458/2022, beneficiaries are provided ₹5,000/- for home decoration upon completion of the house.

faqs.question: Can someone who already owns a house apply?
faqs.answer: No. Applicants should not own a house in their name or in the name of any family member anywhere in India.

faqs.question: What is the maximum annual family income to be eligible?
faqs.answer: The total annual income of the family should not exceed ₹3 lakh.

faqs.question: Can applicants who have received benefits from other housing schemes apply?
faqs.answer: No. Applicants who have availed benefits under any other Central, State, or externally aided housing scheme are not eligible.

faqs.question: Is it necessary to have land to apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. Applicants must have a legally owned plot of land or an existing kutcha/weak house for constructing a pucca house.

faqs.question: How are beneficiaries selected?
faqs.answer: Selection is done after verifying all documents and records. Details are recorded on the official PMAY-U portal, and a survey code is issued for each registered demand.

faqs.question: Where is the application registered?
faqs.answer: Applications are registered at the Municipal Body office of the applicant’s city, and the details are uploaded on [www.pmaymis.gov.in.](https://pmaymis.gov.in/)

faqs.question: Is there a fee to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No. The application process is completely free of charge.

scheme.name: Self-Employment Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Tribes
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to support scheduled castes and scheduled tribes families below the poverty line through concessional loans and subsidies for self-employment in various sectors.
scheme.details:
The "Self-Employment Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Tribes" scheme by the Social Welfare Department, Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to promote self-employment and sustainable livelihood among scheduled caste/ scheduled tribe families living below the poverty line. Under this scheme, provides loans through various banks to scheduled caste families living below the poverty line for projects up to ₹20,000 to ₹7,00,000/- in agriculture, services, business, and transport. The scheme offers a government subsidy of 50% of the project cost or a maximum of ₹10,000/-.

> **Illustrative Ventures:**

Agricultural Equipment, Automobile Workshops, Band Parties, Orchestras, Beauty Parlors, Bicycle Repair, Biogas Plants, Barber Shops, Bookbinding, Brick Making, Bullock Carts, Cable Tv, Candle Making, Greeting Card Making, Carpet Industry, Cloth Business, Copper Industry, Departmental Stores, Dhabas and Restaurants, Driving Schools, Fruit and Flower Production, Flour and Rice Mills, Goat Rearing, Bakeries, General Stores (Pansari Ki Dukan), Hosiery, Bamboo Furniture Making, Wooden Furniture Making, Leather Goods Manufacturing, Shoe Making, Cement Block Making, Beekeeping, Nursing Homes, Poultry Farming, Printing Presses, Pottery Work, Sweet Shops, Tailoring Shops, Tire Servicing, Lamination, PCO/STD Booths, Tent Houses, Auto-taxis, Marble Polishing, Sale and Repair of Electrical Goods, Fast Food Shops, Etc.
scheme.benefits:
> **Financial Assistance:**

- **Loan Amount:** Project loans from ₹20,000/- to ₹7,00,000/- through nationalized banks.- **Subsidy:** 50% of the project cost or up to ₹10,000/- as government subsidy.- **Margin Money:** 25% of project cost provided at 4% annual interest.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must belong to a Scheduled Castes and Tribes community.
1. The applicant must be living below the poverty line.
1. The applicant annual income must not exceed ₹15,975/- in rural areas and ₹21,206/- in urban areas.
1. The applicant must not be a defaulter of any bank or financial institution.
1. The applicant must not have availed any subsidy from any government scheme earlier.
1. The applicant must possess a commercial driving license.

application_process.steps:
> ***Application Process:***

**Step 1:** The interested applicant downloads the [application form](http://www.ukbvvn.org.in/Download/SES_loan_form.pdf) from the official website.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the Village Development Officer/Assistant Social Welfare Officer/Block Development Officer.

> ***Selection Process:***

**Rural Areas:** Beneficiaries are selected through open meetings in Gram Sabha.
**Urban Areas:** Selection is done through interviews.

faqs.question: Who can apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only Scheduled Caste individuals living below the poverty line in Uttarakhand.

faqs.question: Is there any subsidy provided?
faqs.answer: Yes, up to 50% of the project cost or a maximum of ₹10,000.

faqs.answer: 25% of the project cost provided at 4% interest rate by the Corporation.

faqs.answer: Agriculture, service, business, transport sectors are covered.

faqs.answer: Yes, a project proposal must be submitted.

faqs.answer: There is no application fee.

scheme.name: Financial Assistance for Natural Disaster
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide timely financial assistance and relief to individuals and families affected by natural calamities, helping them recover from losses to life, property, and livelihood.
scheme.details: The scheme “Financial Assistance for Natural Disaster” was introduced by the Department of Revenue, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide timely financial assistance and relief to individuals and families affected by natural calamities, helping them recover from losses to life, property, and livelihood.
scheme.benefits: Under this scheme, in case of any loss due to a natural calamity, financial assistance of up to ₹10,000/- is sanctioned by the Tehsildar, up to ₹50,000/- by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, and above ₹50,000/- by the District Magistrate.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a permanent resident of Uttarakhand.
2. The applicant or their family must have been affected by a natural disaster.

application_process.steps:
- In the event of a disaster, upon suo motu cognizance by the Revenue Administration, or on the report of an affected individual, person from the disaster-affected area, or public representative, the revenue officials of the concerned area such as the Patwari, Kanungo, or Tehsildar will inform the officials of the Disaster Department, such as the District Disaster Management Officer. Subsequently, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate or Tehsildar, after conducting a field investigation through the Regional Revenue Sub-Inspector and related departments, will assess the damage and initiate necessary action to provide relief to the affected individual or family as per the prescribed rules.
 - To identify completely damaged buildings, a three-member committee will be constituted at the District Magistrate level, comprising the Block Development Officer (or their representative) and one Junior Engineer. The committee will approve the relief amount for all buildings deemed completely damaged and unsafe for human habitation and will sanction the relief amount for the affected individual or family accordingly.
 - If the financial assistance amount is up to ₹10,000/-, it is approved by the Tehsildar; if it exceeds ₹10,000/- but is below ₹50,000/-, it is approved by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate; and if it exceeds ₹50,000/-, it is approved by the District Magistrate.
 - Currently, the distribution of financial assistance for natural calamities is conducted offline. However, the approval process at the office level has been made online through the [Apuni Sarkar Portal](https://eservices.uk.gov.in/). Once the approval is granted at the District Magistrate level, the sanctioned amount is sent to the Tehsildar through the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, who then forwards it to the concerned Patwari. The Revenue Sub-Inspector (Patwari/Lekhpal) subsequently disburses the amount to the disaster-affected person or family in the respective area. - After approval from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate or Tehsildar, the financial assistance is provided to the person or family affected by the natural calamity through the Revenue Sub-Inspector (Patwari/Lekhpal) of the concerned area.

documents_required: Documents are required as per the guidelines of the Revenue Administration to avail the benefits of the scheme.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only residents of Uttarakhand whose life, property, or livelihood has been affected by a natural disaster are eligible for financial assistance under this scheme.

faqs.question: What is the amount of financial assistance provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer:
Financial assistance is determined based on the extent of damage:

- Up to ₹10,000 – sanctioned by the Tehsildar
- ₹10,001 to ₹50,000 – sanctioned by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM)
- Above ₹50,000 – sanctioned by the District Magistrate (DM)

faqs.question: How is the damage assessment carried out?
faqs.answer: Damage assessment is conducted by the Regional Revenue Sub-Inspector and related departments through a field investigation under the supervision of the Tehsildar or Sub-Divisional Magistrate.

faqs.question: Who initiates the process of providing assistance?
faqs.answer: The process can be initiated either suo motu by the Revenue Administration or based on a report submitted by the affected person, a public representative, or local officials from the disaster-affected area.

faqs.question: How are completely damaged buildings identified?
faqs.answer: A three-member committee headed by the District Magistrate, including the Block Development Officer (or representative) and one Junior Engineer, identifies and verifies buildings that are completely damaged and unsafe for habitation.

faqs.question: What is the procedure after the damage is assessed?
faqs.answer: After assessment, a report is prepared and submitted to the competent authority (Tehsildar/SDM/DM), who approves the relief amount as per the prescribed limits and guidelines.

faqs.question: How is the approved financial assistance amount disbursed?
faqs.answer: Once approved, the amount is sent from the District Magistrate to the Tehsildar through the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, and the Revenue Sub-Inspector (Patwari/Lekhpal) distributes the amount to the affected person or family.

scheme.name: Freeship less than ₹1,00,000 (UG students only)
scheme.brief_description: The scheme "Freeship Less than ₹1,00,000 only for UG students" by the Dean Student Welfare, GBPUAT, Pantnagar aims to support meritorious undergraduate students from low-income families. This Freeship scheme provides full tuition fee exemption to eligible students.
scheme.details: "Freeship Less than ₹1,00,000" Scheme by the Dean Student Welfare, Govind Ballabh Pant Krishi Evam Praudyogiki Vishwavidyalaya, Government of Uttarakhand, aims to provide financial assistance to meritorious undergraduate students from economically weaker backgrounds. Through this scheme, a full tuition fee waiver is granted to selected students whose annual family income is less than ₹1,00,000. The benefit is especially extended to girls for an additional academic year. The scheme is implemented by the Office of the Dean Student Welfare in accordance with university regulations. Applications are scrutinized and the final list is approved by university authorities.
scheme.benefits:
Eligible students get a 100% tuition fee waiver.

Aims to reduce the financial burden on low-income families and encourage academic excellence.

The fee waiver is directly applied during fee processing.

Granted once every academic year, at the beginning of the session.

Disbursed after the final selection list is approved by the Registrar and Vice Chancellor.

Validity:

Boys: Up to 3 academic years

Girls: Up to 4 academic years
scheme.eligibility:

- The applicant’s annual family income should be less than ₹1,00,000.
- The applicant must be among the best-performing students as per the university’s merit guidelines.
- The applicant must submit the application in the prescribed format within the deadline.

application_process.steps:
Step 1: Applications are invited on a prescribed form from eligible and meritorious students.

Step 2: Based on the applications, the Dean Student Welfare prepares a list following the prescribed procedure.

Step 3: The list is forwarded to the Registrar and Vice Chancellor for approval.

Step 4: Once approved, the final list of selected students is issued by an office order.

Step 5: Approved students receive the tuition fee exemption accordingly

Income Certificate (Issued by a Competent Government Authority)
Bank Account Details (Passbook Copy or Cancelled Cheque)

faqs.answer: Undergraduate students whose family income is below ₹1,00,000 per year are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: Is the scheme open to postgraduate or Ph.D. students?
faqs.answer: No, this scheme is exclusively for undergraduate students.

faqs.question: What benefit does the scheme provide?
faqs.answer: Eligible students receive a 100% tuition fee waiver.

faqs.question: How long is the tuition fee waiver applicable?
faqs.answer: For boys, it is valid for 3 academic years; for girls, it extends to 4 academic years.

faqs.answer: Yes, students must submit the university’s prescribed application form.

faqs.answer: The waiver is applied at the start of the academic session, after final selection approval.

scheme.name: Special Incentive Scheme for Women of Tharu, Boksa and Other Tribes (For Training and Marketing)
scheme.department: Uttarakhand Micro, Small And Medium Enterprises
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to empower tribal women artisans through specialized training and marketing opportunities and ensures the provision of financial assistance for travel, logistics, and stall rent for participating artisans.
scheme.details: The “Special Incentive Scheme for Women of Tharu, Boksa and Other Tribes (For Training and Marketing)” is implemented by the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Department under the Department of Industries, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to empower tribal women artisans through specialized training and marketing opportunities and ensures the provision of financial assistance for travel, logistics, and stall rent for participating artisans.
scheme.benefits:
***Training Incentives:***

 - Training is provided in various crafts based on market demand, along with popular crafts traditionally practiced by Tharu, Boxa, and other tribal women.
 - The duration of the training program is two months, with a maximum of 25 training days per month. Each participant undergoes 5 hours of training per day, making a total of 250 training hours for the entire program.

***Marketing Promotions:***

 - Artisans are given priority participation in traditional fairs, exhibitions, and district-level handloom exhibitions organized at the district level.
 - For marketing promotion, the Government of India and the State Government provide space for the display and sale of products created by artisans during various programs, exhibitions, and India International Trade Fairs organized from time to time within the state and across the country.
 - The minimum travel fare for women participating in these exhibitions/fairs, maximum freight of ₹1,000/- per artisan for transporting their products, and stall rent are all borne by the State Government.
scheme.eligibility: 1. Women artisans belonging to the Tharu, Boksa, and other tribes engaged in the craft sector in Uttarakhand will be eligible for training and marketing support.

application_process.steps:
- Application forms can be obtained from the office of the General Manager, District Industries Centre, or downloaded from the departmental website [https://doi.uk.org](https://doi.uk.gov.in/). - Along with the application form, applicants must submit the following documents to the General Manager, District Industries Centre of the respective district: Aadhaar card, bank account details, mobile number, caste certificate, proof of being a craftsman, and an application requesting training or participation in fairs, or a certificate of registration with the Industries Office.

***Selection Process:***

 - The applications received are reviewed by a committee headed by the General Manager, District Industries Centre. Based on the committee’s recommendations, the Director of the Industries Department approves the selection of eligible artisans. After approval, the selected women are invited for training and participation in fairs.

documents_required: Application requesting training or participation in fairs
Certificate of registration with the Industries Office (if applicable)

faqs.question: Who are the beneficiaries of this scheme?
faqs.answer: Women artisans belonging to the Tharu, Boksa, and other tribal communities working in the craft sector in Uttarakhand are eligible beneficiaries.

faqs.question: What kind of training is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Training is provided in various crafts based on market demand, along with traditional crafts practiced by Tharu, Boksa, and other tribal women.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the training program?
faqs.answer: The training program lasts for two months, with a maximum of 25 days per month and 5 training hours per day, totaling 250 hours of training.

faqs.question: What support is provided for marketing and exhibitions?
faqs.answer: Eligible artisans are given priority participation in traditional fairs, exhibitions, and district handloom fairs organized at the district or state level to market their handmade products.

faqs.question: How does the government support artisans during these exhibitions?
faqs.answer: The State Government and the Government of India provide free space for display and marketing of products at exhibitions and trade fairs, such as the India International Trade Fair.

faqs.question: Are travel and logistics expenses covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scheme covers the minimum travel fare, up to ₹1,000 per artisan for transporting products, and also bears the stall rent on behalf of the artisans.

faqs.question: Where can artisans obtain the application form?
faqs.answer: Application forms are available at the office of the General Manager, District Industries Centre, or can be downloaded from the departmental website [https://doi.uk.org](https://doi.uk.gov.in/).

faqs.question: Where should the application form be submitted?
faqs.answer: The completed application form, along with the required documents, should be submitted to the General Manager, District Industries Centre of the concerned district.

faqs.question: What is the process of selection?
faqs.answer: Applications are reviewed by a committee headed by the General Manager, District Industries Centre, and the Director of Industries Department approves the final list of eligible artisans for training and marketing programs.

scheme.name: Bakri Palan Yojana
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to promote goat rearing as a source of self-employment and livelihood generation for eligible beneficiaries, particularly from SECC categories, by providing financial support for rearing a goat unit.
scheme.details: The scheme "Bakri Palan Yojana" was introduced by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote goat rearing as a source of self-employment and livelihood generation for eligible beneficiaries, particularly from SECC categories, by providing financial support for rearing a goat unit.
scheme.benefits:
- Self-employment in goat rearing is facilitated by providing beneficiaries with a goat unit comprising 10 female goats and 1 male goat for a period of 10 to 14 months. 
 - The total cost of the unit is ₹70,000/-, of which 90% (₹63,000/-) is funded by the State Government, and the remaining 10% (₹7,000/-) is contributed by the beneficiary.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must belong to the General, Scheduled Caste, or Scheduled Tribe category.
1. The applicant must be included in the SECC (Socio-Economic and Caste Census) category.
1. The applicant should have an interest in goat rearing.

application_process.steps:

scheme.name: Assistance to Handloom Artisans - Uttarakhand

scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide financial support to disaster-affected handloom artisans for the repair or repurchase of damaged tools, equipment, raw materials, and finished products.
scheme.details: The scheme “Assistance to Handloom Artisans” is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority under the Department of Disaster Management, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide financial support to disaster-affected handloom artisans for the repair or repurchase of damaged tools, equipment, raw materials, and finished products.
scheme.benefits:
**Under this scheme, the following assistance is provided to disaster-affected artisans:**

- **For the repurchase of damaged tools and equipment:** ₹ 5,000/- per artisan for the repurchase of tools. - **For damage to raw materials or products under production or finished:** ₹ 5,000/- per artisan for raw materials.
scheme.eligibility:

application_process.steps:
Information about the disaster and the resulting damage is received from various sources. The concerned Patwari verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form. Once the District Magistrate’s approval is received, relief funds are disbursed to the concerned beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.

Verification report of damage and its replacement, duly certified by the competent authority appointed by the State Government

Financial assistance is provided for:

scheme.name: Rajya/Mukhyamantri Swarn/Rajat Padak Protsahan Puraskar
scheme.brief_description: This scheme awards cash incentives to NCC cadets who demonstrate outstanding performance in the current year's RDC, TSC, VSC, or NSC camps, recognizing six gold medal recipients with ₹3,000/- and six silver medal recipients with ₹2000/-.
scheme.details: "Rajya / Mukhyamantri Swarn / Rajat Padak Protsahan Puraskar" implemented by the Department of Education, Government of Uttarakhand, aims to promote excellence in National Cadet Corps (NCC) training by incentivizing high-performing cadets. Through this scheme, cadets who win gold or silver medals during RDC (Republic Day Camp), TSC (Thal Sainik Camp), VSC (Vayu Sainik Camp), or NSC (Nav Sainik Camp) are awarded cash prizes. The scheme is implemented by NCC Group Headquarters through a structured selection and recommendation process.
scheme.benefits: - **Gold Medal Winners:** A cash award of ₹3,000/- each is given to 6 cadets who achieve gold medals during NCC training and camps.- **Silver Medal Winners:** A cash award of ₹2,000/- each is given to 6 cadets who achieve silver medals during NCC training and camps.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be an NCC cadet.
 1. The applicant must have demonstrated outstanding performance in one of the following camps during the current training year: RDC (Republic Day Camp), TSC (Thall Sainik Camp), VSC (Vayu Sena Camp), or NSC (Nau Sainik Camp).
 1. The applicant must be among the top 6 performers for the gold medal or the next 6 performers for the silver medal.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** Application forms are filled by all NCC Units.
**Step 2:** Filled applications are forwarded by the Units to the Group Headquarters.
**Step 3:** Group Headquarters conducts necessary verification.
**Step 4:** After verification, Group Headquarters sends the applications to the Directorate.
**Step 5:** At the Directorate, a Board of Officers is formed to scrutinize the applications and related documents/board proceedings.
**Step 6:** Based on performance and scrutiny, cash awards are allocated to the top 6 cadets (gold) and next 6 cadets (silver).

faqs.question: What is the purpose of the "Rajya/Mukhyamantri Swarn/Rajat Padak Protsahan Puraskar" scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Rajya/Mukhyamantri Swarn/Rajat Padak Protsahan Puraskar" scheme has been introduced to recognize and encourage exceptional performance by NCC cadets who secure medals during various national-level training camps conducted in the current training year.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to receive the cash incentive under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only those NCC cadets who are actively participating in the current training year and have secured either a gold or silver medal during camps such as the Republic Day Camp (RDC), Thal Sainik Camp (TSC), Vayu Sainik Camp (VSC), or Nav Sainik Camp (NSC) are eligible to receive the cash incentive.

faqs.question: How much monetary reward is given under this scheme to gold medal winners?
faqs.answer: Under this scheme, each NCC cadet who is selected as a gold medal recipient is awarded a monetary prize of ₹3,000/- in recognition of their outstanding performance during training.

faqs.question: What is the amount of reward provided to silver medal-winning cadets?
faqs.answer: NCC cadets who have secured silver medals in the mentioned training camps are awarded a cash incentive of ₹2,000 under the scheme as a form of encouragement and acknowledgment of their efforts.

faqs.question: How many NCC cadets are selected annually for the gold and silver medal rewards?
faqs.answer: A total of 12 NCC cadets are selected each year for this reward, out of which 6 cadets are chosen for the gold medal category and 6 cadets are selected for the silver medal category.

faqs.question: Are cadets from all NCC units within the state eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, cadets from all recognized NCC units operating under the jurisdiction of Uttarakhand are eligible to apply for and benefit from this scheme if they meet the prescribed eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: What are the main camps considered for medal-based selection under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The main camps considered for evaluating and selecting cadets for this award include the Republic Day Camp (RDC), Thal Sainik Camp (TSC), Vayu Sainik Camp (VSC), and Nav Sainik Camp (NSC), where cadets must have won medals.

faqs.question: Is there any online application process available for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the application process for this scheme is entirely offline and involves submitting physical application forms and supporting documents through the concerned NCC units and Group Headquarters.

faqs.question: How is the final list of awardees prepared and approved?
faqs.answer: The final list of awardees is prepared based on merit, evaluated by the Board of Officers constituted by the Directorate, and includes only those cadets who obtain the highest scores in performance and meet all eligibility norms.

faqs.question: When is the cash award generally disbursed to the selected cadets?
faqs.answer: The disbursement of the cash award generally takes place after all applications are scrutinized, approved by the Directorate, and the funds are released to the selected cadets through the respective NCC authorities.

scheme.name: E-Rickshaw Kalyan Yojana
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to promote self-employment among unemployed youth in the state by providing affordable loans for purchase of e-rickshaws, thereby enhancing their livelihoods. Under this scheme, loans are provided to unemployed youth for purchase of e-rickshaws at an annual interest rate of 9%.
scheme.details: The scheme “E-Rickshaw Kalyan Yojana” was launched by the Cooperative Department, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote self-employment among unemployed youth in the state by providing affordable loans for the purchase of e-rickshaws, thereby enhancing their livelihoods.
scheme.benefits:
- Under this scheme, loans are provided to unemployed youth for the purchase of e-rickshaws at an annual interest rate of 9%. Additionally, under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, savings account holders receive an insurance cover of ₹2.00 lakh for an annual premium of ₹12/-. 
 - Beneficiaries aged between 18 and 50 can also avail benefits under the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana by paying a premium of ₹330/- through their savings accounts.
scheme.eligibility:
- The applicant must be a permanent resident of Uttarakhand.
- The applicant should be currently unemployed.
- The applicant must possess a valid driving license.
- The applicant must not be more than 55 years of age.

application_process.steps:
- To obtain a loan for purchasing an e-rickshaw, applicant must visit the nearest cooperative bank and collect the application form. It is mandatory for the applicant to open an account with the respective cooperative bank, and both the applicant and two guarantors must be designated as nominal members of the bank.
 - The application form must be submitted along with the following documents: a dealer’s quotation, details of two guarantors, a permanent residence certificate, Aadhaar card, bank account statement from the relevant bank, voter ID card with a local address, electricity or water bill in the applicant’s name, and a valid driving license. Unemployed individuals residing in urban, semi-urban, or rural areas who are renting a house must also provide a tenancy certificate along with the Uttarakhand Permanent Resident Certificate.
 - Once the application and documents are submitted, the bank reviews and approves the loan. Upon approval, the bank disburses the funds directly to the dealer. The applicant is then required to repay the loan in daily or monthly installments, along with interest at an annual rate of 9%.

documents_required: Bank account statement from the relevant cooperative bank
Voter ID card with local address
Electricity bill or water bill in the applicant’s name
Tenancy certificate (for applicants renting a house)
Uttarakhand Permanent Resident Certificate (mandatory for all applicants)

faqs.question: Who can benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Unemployed youth who are permanent residents of Uttarakhand, aged below 55 years, and possessing a valid driving license are eligible.

faqs.question: What is the purpose of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to enhance livelihoods by supporting self-employment and entrepreneurship through the purchase of e-rickshaws.

faqs.question: What is the interest rate on the loan?
faqs.answer: Loans are provided at an annual interest rate of 9%.

faqs.question: How can I apply for a loan under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants must visit the nearest cooperative bank, obtain the application form, open an account, and submit the required documents.

faqs.question: Is there any insurance benefit under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, savings account holders receive an insurance cover of ₹2.00 lakh for an annual premium of ₹12/-. Additionally, beneficiaries aged 18–50 can avail of Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima by paying a premium of ₹330/-.

faqs.question: Can applicants from rural areas apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, unemployed youth from urban, semi-urban, and rural areas are eligible.

faqs.question: How will the loan amount be disbursed?
faqs.answer: Upon approval, the bank disburses the loan amount directly to the dealer from whom the e-rickshaw is purchased.

scheme.name: Incentives by MSME Department for Setting Up of Aromatic Industries in Aroma Park located at SIIDCUL, Kashipur - Centre for Aromatic Plants
scheme.department: Centre For Aromatic Plants, Selaqui, Dehradun
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to promote the establishment and growth of aromatic industries in Aroma Park, SIIDCUL, Kashipur by providing financial incentives, concessional facilities, and technical support to entrepreneurs, thereby fostering industrial development and economic growth in the region.
scheme.details: The “Incentives by MSME Department for Setting Up of Aromatic Industries in Aroma Park located at SIIDCUL, Kashipur” scheme is implemented by the Centre for Aromatic Plants (CAP), Selaqui, Dehradun, under the Department of Horticulture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote the establishment and growth of aromatic industries in Aroma Park, SIIDCUL, Kashipur by providing financial incentives, concessional facilities, and technical support to entrepreneurs, thereby fostering industrial development and economic growth in the region.
scheme.benefits:
Under this scheme, industries to be set up in Aroma Park are provided with investment promotion assistance, interest subsidy, reimbursement of SGST, exemption from stamp duty, exemption from market fees, and supply of electricity at concessional rates, as detailed in the table below:
**Sr. No.****Criteria****Incentives for units to be set up**1Investment promotion assistance40% (maximum ₹40 lakh) on the fixed capital investment made in plant and machinery and workshop building of the enterprise2Interest Subsidy10% of the interest payable on term loans taken for construction of workshop building and purchase of plant & machinery for a period of 5 years from the date of commencement of production (maximum ₹8 lakh per year per unit)3Reimbursement of SGST100% of the net SGST liability on sales made to customers within the state (B2C) for a period of 5 years from the date of commencement of production4Exemption from Stamp DutyFull exemption from stamp duty charges payable on registration of sale deed/lease deed for land for establishment of the enterprise5Exemption from Market Fee100% exemption from market fee on raw materials for a period of 5 years from the date of commencement of production6Supply of Electricity at Concessional RatesFor a period of 5 years from the date of commencement of production, electricity will be supplied at concessional rates applicable for irrigation/tubewell (currently ₹1.55 per unit) along with uninterrupted supply
scheme.eligibility: 1. Entrepreneurs/ individuals interested in setting up an aromatic industry in Aroma Park will be eligible under this scheme.

application_process.steps:
- For the establishment of aromatic industries in Aroma Park, SIIDCUL invites online applications through advertisements posted on its website: [https://esiidcul.com/eprocure/home](https://esiidcul.com/eprocure/home). Applications for vacant plots in Aroma Park are open for a fixed period. Details regarding plot sizes and the Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) are available on the SIIDCUL website. - Applicants can apply online for their preferred plot based on the plot size and submit the required EMD. After considering all applications received for specific plots within the specified period, industrial plots will be allotted, subject to availability, following the procedure outlined by SIIDCUL. Online bidding is conducted, and the highest bidder is awarded the plot. The successful applicant is issued an allotment letter.
 - More information about vacant plots and advertisements can be obtained from w[ww.siidcul.com](https://siidcul.com/). The Centre for Aromatic Plants (CAP) provides technical assistance to entrepreneurs interested in setting up industries in Aroma Park.

documents_required: Documents are required as per SIIDCUL guidelines to avail the benefits of the scheme.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Entrepreneurs or individuals interested in setting up an aromatic industry in Aroma Park, SIIDCUL, Kashipur, are eligible to avail of the scheme benefits.

faqs.question: What types of incentives are provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer:
The scheme provides:

- Investment promotion assistance
- Interest subsidy on term loans
- Reimbursement of SGST
- Exemption from stamp duty
- Exemption from market fees
- Electricity supply at concessional rates

faqs.question: What is the Investment Promotion Assistance offered?
faqs.answer: 40% of the fixed capital investment made in plant and machinery and workshop building of the enterprise is provided as assistance, up to a maximum of ₹40 lakh.

faqs.question: How does the SGST reimbursement work?

faqs.question: How can one apply for a plot in Aroma Park?

faqs.question: What information is required to apply?
faqs.answer: Applicants need to select their preferred plot size and submit the Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) online as specified in the advertisement.

faqs.question: How are plots allotted?
faqs.answer: Industrial plots are allotted based on the online bidding process. The highest bidder is awarded the plot, subject to availability, following the process outlined by SIIDCUL.

faqs.question: When is the allotment letter issued?
faqs.answer: The successful applicant is issued an allotment letter after the completion of the bidding and selection process.

faqs.question: Where can one find details about vacant plots?

scheme.name: Tubewell Installation /Pond Construction
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to enhance irrigation facilities for farmers in Uttarakhand by providing financial assistance for the construction of tubewells and ponds, thereby improving water availability, supporting horticultural development, and increasing agricultural productivity.
scheme.details: The scheme “Tubewell Installation/ Pond Construction” is implemented by the Department of Horticulture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to enhance irrigation facilities for farmers in Uttarakhand by providing financial assistance for the construction of tubewells and ponds, thereby improving water availability, supporting horticultural development, and increasing agricultural productivity.
scheme.benefits: Under this scheme, to promote the development of irrigation facilities, farmers are provided a 50% subsidy on the total cost for the construction of new tubewells or ponds, up to a maximum of ₹90,000/- per unit (limited to one unit per farmer).
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a farmer and must hold a valid Udhyan Card.
1. The farmer must either own agricultural land or have land on lease.
1. The farmer must confirm the availability of water in the concerned area.
1. A farmer is eligible for a subsidy for the construction of one tube well/pond.

application_process.steps:
- The application form can be obtained from the officers/personnel working at the Horticulture Mobile team Centres. It can also be downloaded from the department's website: [https://shm.uk.gov.in](https://shm.uk.gov.in/). Along with the application form/proposal, the applicant must submit land-related documents such as Khasra and Khatauni, a lease certificate (in case of leased land), Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Udhyan Card, bank account details, and mobile number. At present, the application process is offline. - If the applicant faces any difficulty while completing the application, the personnel at the concerned Horticulture Mobile team Centre will provide assistance. The completed application form must be submitted at the same office. The personnel at the Horticulture Mobile team Centre then forward the proposal to the district level, which further forwards it to the Directorate. After the Directorate approves the farmers’ proposals, an approval/work order is issued to the respective districts.
 - Once a farmer’s proposal is approved, the district officer sends an acceptance letter and also informs the farmer over the phone. The farmer then begins constructing the tube well/pond, after which an on-site inspection is conducted by departmental personnel. Based on the inspection report, the subsidy amount is transferred directly to the farmer’s bank account.

documents_required: Land-related documents such as Khasra and Khatauni
Lease certificate (in case of leased land)

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers who are residents of Uttarakhand, hold a valid Udhyan Card, and have their own land or leased land are eligible.

faqs.question: How much subsidy is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive 50% subsidy of the total cost, up to ₹90,000 per unit, for constructing one tubewell or pond.

faqs.question: How many tubewells or ponds can a farmer construct under the scheme?
faqs.answer: A farmer is eligible for subsidy for only one unit (either one tubewell or one pond).

faqs.question: Do farmers need to verify water availability?
faqs.answer: Yes. The farmer must confirm whether water is available in the proposed area for tubewell installation or pond construction.

faqs.question: Where can farmers get the application form?
faqs.answer: The form can be obtained from Horticulture Mobile Squad Centres or downloaded from the department’s website.

faqs.question: Where should the completed application be submitted?
faqs.answer: The completed form must be submitted at the respective Horticulture Mobile Squad Centre.

faqs.question: How is the application processed after submission?
faqs.answer: The Mobile Squad Centre forwards the proposal to the district level, which then sends it to the Directorate for approval.

faqs.question: How will a farmer know if their proposal is approved?
faqs.answer: Once approved, the district officer sends an acceptance letter and also informs the farmer over the phone.

scheme.name: Free Pre-Recruitment Training

scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide 8 weeks of free pre-recruitment training for recruitment into the Military, Paramilitary, and Police Forces to sons of ex-servicemen aged between 16 and 21 years who have passed high school with at least 45% marks.
scheme.details: The scheme "Free Pre-Recruitment Training" is implemented by the State Sainik Board under the Sainik Welfare Department, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide 8 weeks of free pre-recruitment training for the Military, Paramilitary, and Police forces to the sons of ex-servicemen aged between 16 and 21 years.
scheme.benefits: Under this scheme, 8 weeks of free pre-recruitment training for recruitment into the Military, Paramilitary, and Police Forces is provided to eligible beneficiaries.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a son of an ex-serviceman.
1. The applicant's age should be more than 16 years and less than 21 years.
1. The applicant should have passed high school with 45% marks.

***All expenses incurred on training (honorarium of trainers + food + accommodation) are borne by the Directorate of Sainik Welfare.***
**Note: 5** courses are conducted each year.

application_process.steps:

 - The above documents should be submitted to the concerned District Sainik Welfare Office. Once the applications are processed, selected trainees are informed about the training schedule, after which the training is conducted in the Garhwal and Kumaon divisions of the state.

documents_required: Educational Certificate (at least High School or Higher Secondary)

faqs.question: Who is eligible for this training?
faqs.answer: Sons of ex-servicemen aged 16 to 21 years who have passed High School with at least 45% marks are eligible.

faqs.question: How long is the training program?
faqs.answer: The training program lasts for 8 weeks.

faqs.question: What does the training cover?
faqs.answer: The training prepares candidates for recruitment into Military, Paramilitary, and Police forces, including physical fitness, general knowledge, and written exam preparation.

faqs.question: Are there any charges for the training?
faqs.answer: No. The training is completely free, and all expenses (honorarium of trainers, food, and accommodation) are borne by the Directorate of Sainik Welfare.

faqs.question: How many courses are conducted each year?
faqs.answer: A total of 5 courses are conducted annually.

faqs.question: Where is the training conducted?
faqs.answer: Training is conducted in the Garhwal and Kumaon divisions of Uttarakhand.

faqs.question: How can eligible candidates apply?
faqs.answer: Applications are invited by the District Sainik Welfare Office through public notifications. Candidates must submit their application along with required documents.

faqs.question: Will candidates be informed after selection?
faqs.answer: Yes, participating trainees are informed by the District Sainik Welfare Office before the training begins.

faqs.question: What expenses are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: All training-related expenses including honorarium of trainers, food, and accommodation are provided by the scheme.

faqs.question: Is there any academic qualification requirement?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates must have passed High School with at least 45% marks.

scheme.name: Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families
scheme.department: Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to disaster-affected families for clothes, utensils, or household items in cases where their house has been washed away, completely or substantially damaged due to a natural calamity, or affected by waterlogging for a period of more than two days.
scheme.details: The scheme “Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families” is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority under the Department of Disaster Management, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to disaster-affected families for clothes, utensils, or household items in cases where their house has been washed away, completely or substantially damaged due to a natural calamity, or affected by waterlogging for a period of more than two days.
scheme.benefits: Under this scheme, an ex-gratia grant of ₹2,500/- per family is provided for damage to clothes, and an additional ex-gratia grant of ₹2,500/- per family is provided for damage to utensils or household items.
scheme.eligibility: 1. The beneficiary must be a disaster-affected family from Uttarakhand whose house has been affected by a natural disaster.

application_process.steps: Information about the disaster and the resulting damage is received from various sources. The concerned Patwari verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form. The Patwari’s report is subsequently verified by the Tehsildar and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Approval is then obtained from the District Magistrate. Once the District Magistrate’s approval is received, relief funds are disbursed to the concerned beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.

documents_required: Form P-20 Entry Confirmation (recorded by the concerned Patwari)

faqs.question: Who is eligible to receive assistance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Families whose houses have been washed away, completely or substantially damaged, or affected by waterlogging for more than two days due to a natural disaster are eligible.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: An ex-gratia grant of ₹2,500 per family is provided for damage to clothes and an additional ₹2,500 per family is provided for damage to utensils or household items.

faqs.question: How are the relief funds distributed to the beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: After approval from the District Magistrate, the relief funds are disbursed to beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.

faqs.question: Is this financial assistance given per person or per family?
faqs.answer: The assistance is provided per family.

faqs.question: Who verifies the damage caused by the disaster?
faqs.answer: The Patwari of the concerned area verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form.

faqs.question: Who gives the final approval for providing financial assistance?
faqs.answer: The District Magistrate gives the final approval for the disbursement of relief funds.

scheme.name: Minority Scholarship Scheme for Class 1 to 10
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to provide scholarships to students belonging to minority communities who are studying in Classes 1 to 10 in any recognized government/non-government educational institution in Uttarakhand.
scheme.details: The “Minority Scholarship Scheme for Class 1 to 10” was launched by the Minority Welfare Department, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide scholarships to students belonging to minority communities who are studying in Classes 1 to 10 in any recognized government/non-government educational institution in Uttarakhand.
scheme.benefits:
At present, the State Government provides the following **monthly scholarships** for students from Class 1 to 10:

- **Class 1 to 5:** ₹50/-- **Class 6 to 8:** ₹80/-- **Class 9 to 10:** ₹120/-
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must belong to a minority community (Muslim, Sikh, Christian, Parsi, Buddhist, or Jain).
1. The applicant must be studying in Classes 1 to 10.
1. The applicant must be enrolled in a recognized government/non-government educational institution in the state of Uttarakhand.

application_process.steps:
- Minority community students studying in Classes 1 to 10 can register at any time through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP 2.0) at [https://scholarships.gov.in](https://scholarships.gov.in/). Registration requires an Aadhaar number and an Aadhaar-linked mobile number. - During registration, students provide basic information such as their name, parents’ names, and educational qualifications. Upon successful registration, a student ID and password are generated. 
 - For applying to the scholarship, the department publishes advertisements in newspapers or on the NSP portal, inviting online applications within a stipulated period. 
 - Students must log in using their registered ID and password or register if not already done, and select their school or institution during the application process.
 - While applying, students are required to upload mandatory documents, including educational certificates, Aadhaar card, bank account linked with Aadhaar, permanent residence certificate, self-declaration certificate of minority community, income certificate, certificate of studying in school, and a passport-size photograph. In addition, offline copies of these documents must be submitted to the school or institution for verification. 
 - Once submitted, the application reaches the school’s Institute Nodal Officer (INO), who verifies the documents and forwards the application to the State Nodal Officer (SNO). The SNO then forwards the applications to the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India after a random selection process (2% of applications). 
 - If all documents and eligibility criteria are verified and found correct, the scholarship amount is directly transferred to the student’s bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

faqs.question: Who can apply for this scholarship?
faqs.answer: Students belonging to minority communities, studying in Classes 1 to 10 in recognized educational institutions of Uttarakhand, are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What are the scholarship amounts provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The monthly scholarship amounts are as follows: Class 1 to 5 – ₹50, Class 6 to 8 – ₹80, and Class 9 to 10 – ₹120.

faqs.question: How can a student register for the scholarship?
faqs.answer: Students can register anytime through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP 2.0) at [www.scholarships.gov.in](https://scholarships.gov.in/) using their Aadhaar number and an Aadhaar-linked mobile number.

faqs.question: What information is required during registration?
faqs.answer: During registration, students must provide basic details such as their name, parents’ names, educational qualifications, and other personal information.

faqs.question: How will students know when to apply for the scholarship?
faqs.answer: The department publishes advertisements in newspapers and on the National Scholarship Portal inviting applications within a specified period.

faqs.question: Do students need to submit physical copies of documents?
faqs.answer: Yes, along with online submission, students must submit offline copies of documents to their school or institution for verification.

faqs.question: How is the scholarship payment made?
faqs.answer: Once the application and documents are verified and eligibility is confirmed, the scholarship amount is directly transferred to the student’s bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

faqs.question: Is Aadhaar mandatory to apply for this scholarship?
faqs.answer: Yes, students must have an Aadhaar number, and their bank account should be linked to Aadhaar.

scheme.name: Dugdh Mulya Protsahan Yojana
scheme.brief_description: The scheme aims to encourage milk production and ensure fair remuneration to cattle farmers by providing financial incentives based on the quality of milk supplied to cooperative societies.
scheme.details: The scheme “Dugdh Mulya Protsahan Yojana” was launched by the Department of Dairy Development, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to encourage milk production and ensure fair remuneration to cattle farmers by providing financial incentives based on the quality of milk supplied to cooperative societies.
scheme.benefits: Under this scheme, in addition to paying the price of milk to cattle farmers who supply milk to milk cooperative societies, an incentive of ₹4.00 per litre or ₹3.00 per litre is also paid, as per the prescribed standards.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a member of a milk-producing cooperative society supplying milk to the society.

application_process.steps:
- Members who supply milk to the cooperative society are paid ₹3.00 per litre for the prescribed standard (7.50% to 7.99% fat-free solids) and ₹4.00 per litre for 8.00% or higher fat-free solids. 
 - The incentive is credited to the milk society members through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into their bank accounts. For this purpose, milk suppliers must provide their bank account details to the cooperative society.

faqs.question: Who can benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Cattle farmers who are members of milk-producing cooperative societies and supply milk to these societies are eligible for the incentives.

faqs.question: What is the incentive provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Members supplying milk receive an additional incentive of ₹3.00 per litre for milk with 7.50% to 7.99% fat-free solids and ₹4.00 per litre for milk with 8.00% or higher fat-free solids.

faqs.question: How is the incentive paid to the farmers?
faqs.answer: The incentive is directly transferred to the bank accounts of the milk suppliers through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

faqs.question: Are there any quality standards for milk to be eligible for the incentive?
faqs.answer: Yes. Milk with 7.50% to 7.99% fat-free solids qualifies for ₹3.00/litre, and milk with 8.00% or higher fat-free solids qualifies for ₹4.00/litre.

faqs.question: Can non-members of milk cooperative societies receive the incentive?
faqs.answer: No.

scheme.name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
scheme.brief_description: The scheme facilitates the annual appointment of contract-based sports coaches to conduct various local training camps across Uttarakhand, thereby promoting employment opportunities and strengthening the state’s grassroots sports infrastructure.
scheme.details: The scheme “Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches” was launched by the Department of Sports, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to appoint sports coaches on a contract basis to ensure the smooth functioning of local training camps for various sports across the state.
scheme.benefits: Every year, around 250 coaches benefit from these training camps and gain employment.
scheme.eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a sportsperson or a coach from Uttarakhand.
 1. The applicant must be between 21 and 70 years of age.
 1. The applicant must possess the relevant educational and sports qualifications.

application_process.steps:
- The department organizes local training camps for various sports every year. To ensure the smooth functioning of these camps, sports coaches are appointed on a contractual basis.
 - At the district level, applications for conducting local training camps are submitted by the District Sports Officers.
 - Each year, a notification regarding the scheme is published in daily newspapers, usually in the month of March. The training camps are then organized for a maximum duration of 11 months, from 15th April to 15th March.

documents_required: Submission of documents is required in accordance with the department's guidelines to avail the benefits of the scheme.

faqs.question: Who can apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible state-level players and qualified sports coaches can apply for contractual appointment.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for the coach to be a permanent resident of Uttarakhand?
faqs.answer: No, it is not mandatory for a contract trainer to be a domicile or permanent resident of Uttarakhand.

faqs.question: What qualifications are required to become a contract sports coach?
faqs.answer: Applicants should have the required educational and sports-related qualifications, as prescribed in the notification issued each year.
